title: Zoning for a glass studio: where an artisan workshop is allowed, the change of use, special use permits and the home-occupation limits
question: I want to open a hot glass studio (furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches) with classes, and maybe a cafe. Which zoning districts allow it, and what zoning approvals do I need before I apply for building permits?
office: Neighborhood Development Services (NDS): Zoning (use determinations, accessory use and temporary use permits) and Development Review (pre-application conferences, development plans, special use permits)
summary: Charlottesville's Development Code (City Code ch. 34, in force since February 19, 2024) lists glass blowing by name as an example of an 'Artisan workshop', a retail-category use permitted by right in every mixed-use and industrial district (CX-3, CX-5, CX-8, NX-3, NX-5, NX-8, NX-10, DX, IX-5, IX-8) and in CM, and not allowed in the residential districts (R-A, RN-A, R-B, R-C, RX-3, RX-5) or CV. A furnace shop does not fit the home-occupation rules, which bar equipment not customarily found in a home, hazardous materials, and any noise or odor beyond the dwelling. Classes, a cafe and events are separate uses to classify with NDS Zoning (a cafe is 'General food and beverage', permitted in the same districts; an event venue is 'General indoor entertainment and recreation'). Look up the parcel in the City GIS Viewer, then ask NDS Zoning for a written determination or a Zoning Compliance Letter (listed at $250 for mixed use and commercial) before signing a lease. Moving a glass studio into an existing building is a 'change of use' under the Code and needs a building permit and a new certificate of occupancy from Building Inspections, but not Development Review unless site access changes. Only if the use is marked 'S' for the district (for example high-impact manufacturing in IX districts) is a Special Use Permit needed: a mandatory pre-application conference, $2,000 per public hearing plus notice costs, a community meeting, Planning Commission and City Council hearings, and the permit lapses after 18 months if unused.

steps.step: Find the zoning district of the site you have in mind
steps.who: Prospective operator (owner, lessee or contract purchaser)
steps.how: Search the address in the City of Charlottesville GIS Viewer (https://gisweb.charlottesville.org/GisViewer/), which shows the zoning district and overlay districts under the Development Code adopted December 18, 2023 and effective February 19, 2024. Check that the address is inside city limits: some Charlottesville mailing addresses are in Albemarle County, which has its own zoning and permits. Note any Architectural Design Control, Historic Conservation or Entrance Corridor overlay, because exterior changes and signs there need a Certificate of Appropriateness.
steps.quote: To determine which zoning district your property is in, search your address in the City of Charlottesville’s GIS Viewer , an interactive overview of the city’s zoning districts.

steps.step: Classify the studio under the Development Code: an Artisan workshop, by right in the mixed-use and industrial districts
steps.how: The Development Code's use definitions name glass blowing as a typical example of an 'Artisan workshop' (§ 3.3.4.H.2), a specific use in the Retail category. In the Permitted Use Table (§ 3.2.2) the artisan workshop row reads P (permitted by right) in CX-3, CX-5, CX-8, NX-3, NX-5, NX-8, NX-10, DX, IX-5 and IX-8 and in CM, and '-' (not allowed) in R-A, RN-A, R-B, R-C, RX-3, RX-5 and CV. No use standards (*) are attached to the row and no size cap is stated. Read the industrial definitions too: 'Low-impact industrial and manufacturing' expects no significant use of highly combustible or flammable gases, and 'High-impact industrial and manufacturing' (which lists production of glass materials or products) is allowed only by Special Use Permit in IX-5 and IX-8. Because a hot shop with a gas-fired furnace, oxygen and propane could be read either way, ask Zoning in writing to confirm the artisan-workshop classification for your equipment list before you commit to a site.
steps.quote: Typical examples include art studio; ceramic manufacturing; glass blowing; jewelry manufacturing; metalwork; musical instrument manufacturing; leatherwork; and woodworking, cabinet makers or furniture manufacturing.

steps.step: Classify the other parts of the business: classes, a cafe, retail sales, events
steps.how: Each principal use on the lot must be permitted in the district. Public classes are not a listed use on their own; the nearest listed uses are 'College, university or vocational school' (post-secondary education, 'artistic or vocational school'), permitted by right in all CX, NX, DX, IX, CV and CM districts, and 'Gym or studio', which the Code defines around fitness classes. Selling finished work on site fits 'General retail' (up to 4,000 SF), by right in RX-3 and RX-5 with use standards and in all CX, NX, DX and IX districts and CM. A cafe is 'General food and beverage' (same districts; the definition says alcohol may only be served for on-premise consumption as an accessory use). A space hired out for events is 'General indoor entertainment and recreation' ('event venue'), by right up to 4,000 SF in the CX, NX, DX and IX districts and CM, and by Special Use Permit in CV. In an RX district commercial uses may not exceed 25% of the floor area on the lot. Ask Zoning which single or combined classification it will apply, because the answer sets the parking, transition and building-code occupancy questions that follow.
steps.quote: A use that provides post-secondary education to students. Typical examples include college or university, community college, seminary, and artistic or vocational school.

steps.step: Rule out the home-occupation route for a furnace shop
steps.how: A home occupation is allowed in every residential district with an Accessory Use Permit ($100 in the NDS Fee Schedule), but the standards in § 3.5.2.D exclude a hot shop: no mechanical or electrical equipment other than what is customarily found in a home; no audible noise, vibration or odor beyond the dwelling; no storage of hazardous materials not customary in a dwelling; no more than 3 customers or clients present at once; and no retail sales picked up on site. The applicant must also show a City business license, proof of taxes paid, and a certificate of occupancy or written confirmation from the building official. A small cold-working or torch studio in a home is a question for Zoning; a gas furnace is not.
steps.quote: More than 3 customers or clients of a home occupation business cannot be present on the premises at the same time.

steps.step: Get the use confirmed in writing: a zoning determination or Zoning Compliance Letter
steps.who: Operator; Zoning Administrator (the Director of NDS or a designee)
steps.how: Email or call NDS Zoning (434-970-3995) with the address, the equipment list (furnace fuel and input, glory hole, kilns, torches, oxygen and propane storage) and the activities (classes, retail, cafe, events). Ask for a written determination of the use classification and whether it is permitted by right. The NDS Fee Schedule lists a 'Zoning Compliance Letter - Mixed Use/Commercial' ($250 as printed; the scanned schedule's rows are hard to align, so confirm the amount). State law gives the zoning administrator 90 days to answer a request for a determination. Written determinations the City has issued are posted on the Zoning Determinations page.
steps.deadline: The zoning administrator must respond within 90 days of a request (Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4))
steps.fee: Zoning Compliance Letter, mixed use/commercial: $250 as printed in the NDS Fee Schedule

steps.step: If the site needs no site changes: treat the move-in as a change of use and go to building permits
steps.who: Operator; NDS Development Review and Building Inspections
steps.how: Under the Code a change of use is any change in the principal use of a building or part of it from one listed use to another, or an increase in intensity. The City says Development Review is not required for a change of use unless site access changes or new access improvements are needed; such projects go straight to building-permit review, where zoning compliance is checked with the permit. The USBC requires a permit application when a change of occupancy needs a new certificate of occupancy, and no occupancy or change of occupancy is allowed before the certificate is issued. The Development Code's temporary-use rules also list 'Occupancy permits' among the approvals every activity must hold. See glass_studio_building_mechanical for the permits and inspections.
steps.quote: A change of use does not require Development Review if it does not alter site access or require new access improvements.

steps.step: If you build new, add on, or change the site: Development Review with a pre-application conference
steps.who: Operator and designer; NDS Development Review Team
steps.how: New construction, additions, site modifications and some changes of use go through Development Review (Code § 5.2.9). Applicants must meet the Administrator and the Development Review Team before applying; the meeting is required for Development Plans and Major Final Site Plans and may be required for Minor Final Site Plans. A signed Pre-Application Meeting Acknowledgement form is uploaded with the application. Applications go in through the Cityworks permit portal with the fee, plans and checklists in the Development Review Procedures Manual. Review cycles: Development Plans 21 days for the first three submissions; Minor Final Site Plans three 21-day reviews and a 14-day final. An approved Final Site Plan is required before building permits. Fees (NDS Fee Schedule, March 23, 2026): Development Plan Review $400; Final Site Plan Review Minor $800; Major $1,800 plus $20 per residential unit and $20 per 100 SF of commercial space.
steps.deadline: Development Plans: 21-day review cycles for the first three submissions and 14 days for a fourth; Minor Final Site Plans: three 21-day reviews and a 14-day final review
steps.fee: Development Plan Review $400; Final Site Plan Review (Minor) $800; (Major) $1,800 plus $20 per residential unit and $20 per 100 SF of commercial space
steps.quote: Applicants must meet with the Administrator and Development Review Team before submitting an application. This meeting covers required procedures, standards, and regulations. It is required for all Development Plans and Major Final Site Plans and may be required for Minor Final Site Plans depending on project scope.

steps.step: If the use is marked 'S' for the district: apply for a Special Use Permit
steps.who: Operator; Administrator (staff report); Board of Architectural Review (if in an ADC or HC district or an IPP); Planning Commission (public hearing, recommendation); City Council (decision)
steps.how: A Special Use Permit is needed only where the use table shows S, for example high-impact industrial and manufacturing in IX-5 and IX-8, low-impact industrial and manufacturing over 4,000 SF in CX-3, CX-5, NX-3, NX-5 and NX-8, or an event venue in CV. Steps: a mandatory pre-application conference with the Administrator (waivable at the Administrator's discretion); a complete application with the signed Pre-Application Verification Form, disclosure of real parties in interest, project narrative, Comprehensive Plan analysis, context maps and verification of a community meeting; if the project also needs Development Review, a Development Plan or Final Site Plan must be submitted and commented on first. Staff review takes 30 days for the first submission and 30 days for each resubmission. Nothing is put on a hearing agenda until the community meeting has been held and the NDS Director finds the application ready. The Planning Commission holds a public hearing and recommends; City Council holds a public hearing and decides, and may attach conditions. Council weighs noise, lights, dust, odor, fumes and vibration among the adverse impacts. Fee: $2,000 per public hearing plus mailing ($1.00 per owner notice) and the cost of published notice.
steps.deadline: Staff review: 30 days for the initial submission and 30 days for each resubmission; the SUP expires 18 months after Council approval if the use has not started (or no building permit has been approved)
steps.fee: $2,000 per public hearing, plus mailing costs ($1.00 per owner notice) and the cost of published notice
steps.quote: Special Use Permit requests follow the following review schedule: 30 days for the initial submission, 30 days each for all resubmissions. No application for a Special Use Permit will be placed on any agenda for a public hearing until a required community meeting has been held and the Director of Neighborhood Development Services determines that the application is ready for final review through the formal public hearing process.

steps.step: Plan signs, outdoor events and historic-district work as separate zoning permits
steps.who: Operator; NDS Zoning (sign and temporary use permits); Board of Architectural Review (Certificates of Appropriateness)
steps.how: Most permanent signs need a Sign Permit applied for in the City Permit Portal with size, materials, location, lighting and a site plan ($100 per sign; $200 after the fact); in an ADC, Historic Conservation or Entrance Corridor district a Certificate of Appropriateness replaces it. Small temporary signs up to 10 square feet need no permit; large temporary signs up to 32 square feet need a free permit and are not allowed in R- districts. Outdoor events on the lot (temporary outdoor assemblies, 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, with parking of one space per 4 persons; outdoor sales) need a Temporary Use Permit under Code Div. 3.6 ($250 in the fee schedule; $500 after the fact), limited to 5 per lot per calendar year, 21 days apart, one at a time, set back 20 feet from the right-of-way, and the Administrator may require a bond of up to $100,000. Events on city streets or property go through Parks & Recreation instead (see glass_studio_food_and_events).
steps.fee: Sign Permit or Certificate of Appropriateness for a sign: $100 per sign ($200 after the fact); Temporary Use Permit: $250 ($500 after the fact)
steps.quote: A sign permit is required for a temporary sign, which can be applied for on the City’s Permit Portal (There is no fee for this permit)

steps.step: Keep the zoning approvals current and know the enforcement rules
steps.how: Operate within the use as approved; expanding floor area or intensity (for example more seats in the cafe) is itself a change of use. A Special Use Permit runs with the property and lapses if the use does not begin within 18 months. The business license application warns that the business must be properly zoned before it begins operation. Violations are handled under Code Div. 5.4 (civil penalties of $200 for a first scheduled violation and $500 for later ones; other violations as misdemeanors), and a notice of violation can be appealed to the Board of Zoning Appeals.
steps.quote: Business must be properly zoned before beginning operation (Zoning Department phone # (434) 970-3182).

caveats: The use-table rows were read from the official Development Code PDF (updated March 23, 2026) in raw text order, with the district columns in the order printed in the table header: R-A, RN-A, R-B, R-C, RX-3, RX-5, CX-3, CX-5, CX-8, NX-3, NX-5, NX-8, NX-10, DX, IX-5, IX-8, CV, CM. The quoted rows are the extracted text with single spaces; confirm against the PDF page (Article 3, pages 3-5 to 3-7) before relying on a single cell.

Whether NDS will treat a gas-fired hot shop with oxygen and propane as an 'Artisan workshop' (by right) rather than 'Low-impact' or 'High-impact industrial and manufacturing' is the central open question. The artisan-workshop definition names glass blowing, but the industrial definitions turn on flammable gases and off-premises heat, noise and odor. Only a written determination from NDS Zoning settles it.

Public classes have no exact listed use. 'College, university or vocational school' (post-secondary, 'artistic or vocational school') and 'Gym or studio' (fitness classes) are the closest; Zoning may treat classes as accessory to the workshop. Not confirmed.

The NDS Fee Schedule is a scanned, two-column PDF whose rows do not align cleanly in text extraction. Amounts given here (SUP $2,000 per hearing; Development Plan $400; Final Site Plan Minor $800 / Major $1,800; Accessory Use Permit $100; sign permit $100; temporary use permit $250; Zoning Compliance Letter $250) follow the printed rows as best they can be read. Confirm with NDS before paying.

City Code chapters outside the Development Code (for example the appeal and civil penalty provisions cited by section number) were read only as the Development Code PDF states them; the Municode copy of the City Code was not read because Municode's terms forbid reprinting.
Albemarle County is a separate jurisdiction with its own zoning ordinance; this file covers only sites inside Charlottesville city limits.
The Development Code 'Clean-Up' project (NDS page) may change these sections; the PDF read is the March 23, 2026 update.
